triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The §122 temporary import surcharge was zeroed whenever the entry carried the witness's exemplar-line identity flags entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b — conditions with no basis in any cited provision — instead of when the entry actually fell in the heading 9903.03.03 exclusion list or was a §232-covered aluminum/steel/copper article, the two exceptions the rule's own (unchanged) proof atoms cite, so on generated chapter 86 lines the surcharge was suppressed for every §301-list-1 or aluminum-flagged line regardless of origin; the same exemplar flags also stood in for §232-aluminum, §201 CSPV, China-301 list, Brazil-301 and forced-labor-301 membership.
triage.triage_notes: Reference module for this chunk; indices 85-95 are byte-for-byte the same change modulo chapter prefix, redundant-parenthesis count, and the effective_from/from key spelling used by the placement gate (verified by normalized diff of all 12: identical 9 hunks, 64 added / 19 removed lines each, identical identifier set). Decisive hunk: section_122_component_rate versions[1] (2026-02-24..2026-07-23) goes from 'if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0 else: temporary_import_surcharge_rate' to 'if entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered: 0 ...'; its proof atoms were NOT touched and already cite 'subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03' and 'articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04', so the atoms described the right law and the formula did not implement it. Same commit also: (a) re-grounds §232-aluminum on entry_is_section_232_aluminum and China-301 on per-list membership (line_c -> list4a, line_b -> 2024_action), (b) rewrites brazil_section_301_component_rate and forced_labor_section_301_component_rate from 'exclude exemplar lines a/b, then apply by origin' to 'require list membership AND origin', which additionally adds a list-membership conjunct (unrepresented_clause flavor) while removing the ungrounded exemplar exclusion, (c) the §201 CSPV hunk (entry_is_line_e -> entry_is_section_201_cspv) is semantically inert because both branches return 0, (d) adds section_232_steel_component_rate + chapter-prefixed 0.50 parameter and a new '+ section_232_steel_component_rate' term in schedule_statutory_stack — that addition is new coverage, not a pre-existing defect. Caveats a reviewer should see: at THIS commit the new steel rule's atoms are double-nested under metadata.proof.proof.atoms (so invisible to the proof gate) and cite us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 / .88, which do NOT resolve in the pinned corpus release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap; the PR issue comment records the review repair ('steel atoms unwrapped to canonical metadata.proof.atoms'; '9903.82.02 provision added to every module's source-verification set'), and the later main-line state of this file (checked at 4f591c426) indeed has canonical metadata.proof.atoms citing us/statute/hts/9903.82.02, which resolves to 'Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 50%'. a9562cfd44 is a mid-PR commit (single parent 29dbbdac0), not the merged tip, so those provenance repairs land after it. Decoupling is also incomplete here: post-fix the module still uses entry_is_line_a (1), entry_is_line_b (3, incl. 'if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b' in the IEEPA reciprocal term) and entry_is_line_d (5, incl. a China-301 list-1 term and §338 beer); the summary documents only the line_d/§338 retention.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a mere input-interface generalization and could not: the pre-fix ch86 file proves the defect mechanically, independent of the PR prose. In the parent blob, `entry_is_line_a` is simultaneously the formula of `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` (line 1907) and the §301 list-1 membership gate in `china_section_301_component_rate` (line 2994), while `section_122_component_rate` versions[1] zeroes the 10% surcharge on `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b` (line 2572) with no origin condition — so any chapter-86 line entry-prep flagged as §301 list-1 or aluminum lost the §122 surcharge for every origin, exactly as the PR body states. The rule's own unchanged proof atoms confine the §122 exceptions to "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03", "7202.11.10", and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"; an exemplar-line identity flag is not one of them, so the branch condition had no source basis and the fix re-grounds it on `entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered` — untraceable_branch, not a rename, a policy choice, or added scope.
triage.verifier_notes: Kind runner-up is wrong_entity_or_scope (the condition selects the wrong population of lines), but the taxonomy puts "a condition with no basis in the cited source (the fix removes or re-grounds it)" under untraceable_branch, which is the better fit here: the source states no exception keyed to exemplar-line identity at all. Reviewer cautions on the rest of this same module diff, which is multi-kind and should not be folded into this finding: (1) `section_232_steel_component_rate` + `ch86_s232_steel_heading_rate` are NEW coverage the module never claimed (the pre-fix summary scopes the stack to "the same panel-projection component sequence as the witness total", and the witness's 7202.11.10.00 ferroalloy exemplar sits outside note 16(c)), so that addition alone would be not_a_defect / unclear, not a fidelity fix; (2) the `brazil_section_301_component_rate` and `forced_labor_section_301_component_rate` edits ADD a previously-missing listed-line membership condition (pre-fix they applied the §301 rate to every Brazil-origin / listed-country entry in the chapter), which reads as unrepresented_clause — a separate defect from the pinned §122 one; (3) the decoupling is only partial — post-fix lines 1908, 1925, 2693, 2817, 2873 and 2998 still ride `entry_is_line_a/b/d`, so residual exemplar coupling survives this commit (the summary admits "Beer/section-338 keeps entry_is_line_d because no membership module exists"). Proof atoms and citation paths for §122 are unchanged by the diff, so this is not an excerpt/provenance-only change. I also resolved us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221 through the pinned release (corpus us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, provision sha 818d993e…); the resolved page under HTS 2026 Rev. 3 covers note subdivisions (x)–(z) rather than the (aa)(ii) list the atom spans, i.e. the atom's page anchor does not reproduce under the pinned release — that is a provenance wrinkle worth a separate look, but it does not bear on this kind, which turns on the branch condition rather than on the exclusion list's contents. This module is one of 100 identically generated chapter files in the commit, so the same finding presumably duplicates across the sibling modules.
triage.screen_reason: b1.6 generalize (PR #1300): decouples component gates from exemplar flags; PR body says the witness's exemplar coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — logic/scope correction to 100 merged generated modules.
